title: The Factors that Affect Learning: Evidence - 3: The seven things a learning-focused school really needs evidence about.
author: Martin Skelton
summary: Skelton contrasts coaches, conductors and a rehearsing president, who all study live performance for evidence of improvement, with a teacher whose class is visited briefly by someone with a checklist. His claim is that learning walks and walk-throughs, however relational or useful for culture, are not about learning, and that repeated visits teach staff and students that learning is not what matters most. He argues the most important evidence for a learning-focused school is whether students in classrooms are getting better, and offers a definition of a good teacher built on that outcome. He lays out seven questions, the first four about students and the last three about teacher and school, with follow-up prompts that feed coaching, professional development and school planning. He also lists how gathering this evidence goes wrong, including weak observer understanding, poor interpersonal skills, inspection rather than coaching mode and lack of time.
points: Brief walk-throughs serve relationships and school glue but cannot give evidence about whether students are getting better, and they signal what the school values.
The single most important evidence for a school is what proportion of its classes are places where good learning consistently happens.
Skelton defines a good teacher by whether most students improve academically, emotionally, socially and physically while enjoying it, not by displays, control or hours worked.
Seven questions about learning, appropriateness, sufficiency, engagement, helpful and unhelpful teacher actions and school conditions turn observations into coaching, development and planning.
Evidence gathering fails when observers lack understanding or interpersonal skill, slip into inspection mode, or are short of time.
quotes: If I were appointed to another Headship of a school tomorrow there is one piece of evidence I would want above any other. It is this: What proportion of the classes in my school are places where good learning is consistently happening?

A good teacher is someone who, most of the time, enables the majority of her children or students to get better academically, emotionally, socially and physically and creates a sense of enjoyment and engagement for them in the improvements they are making.
Imagine describing your school or classroom as learning focused and not knowing whether or how getting better is happening or to what extent.

At the risk of sounding simple, this is because students' ability to learn and their enjoyment of getting better is (or should be) at the very heart of what a learning school is about. It’s supposed to be the Hedgehog Concept. If I haven’t got information about that then the rest is no more than data-driven noise.

Easier because like the sports coach, the conductor and the President, the coaching points are directly based on evidence about what is happening in real time. Easier, because the evidence about teachers creates less pressure on them and can often be more celebratory.
